results.snippet: The 10-year U.S. Treasury yield fell below 5% for the first time in a month as a global bond selloff gave way to a flight for safety. Concerns over France’s gaping budget deficit and the risk that rising oil prices could weigh on consumption and economic growth changed the mood in bond markets. French bonds sold off, pushing yields higher, while the opposite happened in bonds perceived as safer, including the German Bunds and the U.S. Treasurys. Copyright ©2026 Dow Jones & Company, Inc.
